answer: Zero-knowledge credential nullifiers resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to privately prove possession of an issuer-signed eID or passport and register one deterministic, domain-scoped nullifier. Because each physical document maps to a single nullifier per registry, attackers cannot grow an orchard of clones from cheap keypairs and must obtain scarce real-world identities. However, illicit brokers can still harbor rented credentials, and issuer revocations move like a glacier.
